desc:
Find the longest contiguous block of s (a substring) that appears in t as a subsequence: its characters occur in t in the same order, but not necessarily next to each other.

Return the length of that block. It is 0 if no single character of s occurs in t (or if either string is empty).

s = "abcab",  t = "xaybzc"  ->  3   ("abc" sits in t as x[a]y[b]z[c])
s = "abcde",  t = "aebdc"   ->  3   ("abc")
s = "abab",   t = "bbaa"    ->  2   ("ba")
constraints: Both strings contain only lowercase English letters
hints: For one fixed start position in s you can extend greedily and match each character to its earliest unused occurrence in t. Doing that for every start is correct but costs O(m · n) per start. Look for a table that reuses work between starts.
Let L[i][j] be the length of the longest suffix of s[0..i) that is a subsequence of t[0..j). If a suffix of some length works, every shorter suffix works too.
If s[i-1] != t[j-1] then L[i][j] = L[i][j-1]. If they are equal, the character can be matched here, so L[i][j] = max(L[i][j-1], L[i-1][j-1] + 1). The answer is the largest L[i][n].
editorial: Because we need a substring of s, it is natural to fix where it ends. Define L[i][j] as the longest suffix of s[:i] that is a subsequence of t[:j]. Note the monotonicity: if a suffix of length k is a subsequence, so is any shorter suffix of it (drop its first characters).

Transition: if the last character s[i-1] differs from t[j-1], t[j-1] cannot help, so L[i][j] = L[i][j-1]. If they are equal, we either do not use t[j-1] (value L[i][j-1]) or match s[i-1] to it, which needs the rest of the suffix to fit into t[:j-1], giving L[i-1][j-1] + 1 by monotonicity. The answer is the maximum of L[i][len(t)] over all i.

Compare with the longest common subsequence (no contiguity in s, so the best value always carries forward from the row above) and with the longest common substring (contiguous in both strings, so a mismatch resets the value to zero). Here the requirement is contiguous in one string only, which gives this hybrid table. Keep one previous row for O(n) memory.
